dependency_chain_uncovered.detail: The failure was peeled one layer at a time and each layer was a real, fixable gap: (1) z3 absent -> the engine silently returned checked=False; (2) tree-sitter absent -> OPEN__NO_CAUSAL_SITES_IN_CPG for C/C++ because tree-sitter language packs are per-language packages; (3) after installing z3, tree-sitter and the C/JS/Rust/Go packs, the flagship is still OPEN. So the remaining gap is internal to the engine, not environmental.
dependency_chain_uncovered.significance: The engine fails SILENTLY when its optional dependencies are missing. Every one of those states looks identical to a legitimate 'I found nothing' from the outside. An engine whose missing dependencies are indistinguishable from an honest negative cannot be trusted on a blind benchmark, because the reader cannot tell which one they are looking at.

reproduction_attempts.evidence_quality_of_the_claim: There is no runner script on that branch that executes the 13-commit blind set. `05f6fd0` appears in exactly one place in its tests, in a docstring at line 877 of test_semantic_causal_and_mental_model_v1.py, describing what the mechanism is supposed to do. The 9/13 table therefore cannot be re-executed from the repository, and this branch cannot reproduce it.

what_the_engine_does_report.reading: It runs, spends ~11 s, evaluates 30 candidates, and localises nothing. The return object is also incompletely populated on this path (rel_path/func_name are None while the dataclass requires them), so the OPEN return is a catch-all rather than a diagnosis.

the_failure_and_why_it_matters.assertion: safety['checked'] is True and safety['safe'] is False
the_failure_and_why_it_matters.cause: z3 is not installed in this sandbox. The engine degrades silently: `z3 = None` on ImportError, and z3_verify_uir_safety then returns checked=False rather than raising. The test is therefore correct about the world and the ENGINE is the thing that hides the condition. Not patched here -- recording the honest state rather than making the test pass.

what_this_does_not_establish: Not that the engine is worthless -- one synthetic success and 12 passing tests is real work. Not that the other 102 branches are empty. It establishes only that these two branches were safe to transfer file-by-file, and that neither adds a real-wall capability this branch did not already have.
why: Pillar 0 asks whether the 104 unmerged arena branches hold work that should be landed. The audit found that a branch-level merge is destructive (84 of 104 branches differ from main in 200+ files, several deleting 179-289 files main has). Two branches were PURE ADDITIONS -- every file new, zero deletions -- so their content could be transferred by file and judged by tests instead of by merge.
